Classic random graph generators

random_graphs.Rd

Fast native C++23 random network generators: Erdos–Renyi \(G(n, p)\) (using Batagelj–Brandes \(O(n + m)\) geometric skipping) and \(G(n, m)\) (Floyd sampling), Barabasi–Albert / Price preferential attachment, Watts–Strogatz small-world lattices, stub-matching configuration models, and planted Stochastic Block Models.

Usage

random_graph_erdos_renyi(n, p = NULL, m = NULL, directed = FALSE,
                         self_loops = FALSE)
random_graph_barabasi_albert(n, m = 2L, gamma = 1.0, directed = FALSE)
random_graph_watts_strogatz(n, k = 4L, p = 0.05, circular = TRUE)
random_graph_configuration(out_deg, in_deg = NULL)
random_graph_sbm(blocks, probs, directed = FALSE, self_loops = FALSE)

Arguments

n

Non-negative number of vertices.

p

Edge probability in \([0, 1]\) for \(G(n, p)\) or shortcut rewiring probability for random_graph_watts_strogatz().

m

Exact number of edges for \(G(n, m)\), or edges added per new vertex in random_graph_barabasi_albert().

directed

Logical; whether the generated graph is directed.

self_loops

Logical; whether self-loops are permitted.

gamma

Preferential-attachment degree exponent \(w_v \propto k_v^\gamma + 1\) (default 1.0 gives linear Barabasi–Albert / Price attachment).

k

Initial lattice degree (rounded down to an even integer 2 * floor(k / 2)) in random_graph_watts_strogatz().

circular

Logical; whether the initial lattice wraps into a ring.

out_deg, in_deg

Non-negative integer degree sequences for stub matching. Omit in_deg for an undirected configuration-model multigraph.

blocks

Positive integer group membership vector of length \(N\).

probs

\(B \times B\) matrix of inter-/intra-block edge probabilities in \([0, 1]\).

Value

An rgraphtool_graph object. random_graph_sbm() also attaches the planted group memberships as vertex property "block".

Examples

set.seed(1)
g_er <- random_graph_erdos_renyi(100L, p = 0.04)
g_ba <- random_graph_barabasi_albert(100L, m = 2L)
g_ws <- random_graph_watts_strogatz(100L, k = 4L, p = 0.1)
